note: Vol. I No. 45. The town is on pages 2 column 6 (the marine list) and 3. This issue prints the 1 October 1834 letter list for the first time, at page 3 columns 1-2, but the segmenter lost its opening and its left sub-column; the names are minted from 1834-10-22, which carries it whole. Page 3 column 2 is the richest advertising column of the month and carries the Democrat's own office at Clark and South Water.

claims.notes: THE PORT IN ONE WEEK: one arrival and eight clearances, seven schooners and a sloop. The marine list column is interleaved with a news column line for line, so `lines_of_claim` names only the shipping lines. Destinations are cut at the column edge on most entries and are left '[…]'; 'Buff[alo]', 'St. J[ose]ph' and 'M[ilwauk]ie' are supplied because the run prints them repeatedly in full. The masters are minted as persons — a master calling at Chicago is not a resident candidate, and none of them is flagged letter_list_only, so the gazetteer holds them on the stronger evidence.

Dr. John T. Temple advertises a store on South Water street in the same issue, so 'Dr. Temple's' on Lake street is a second premises and NOT the same address; both stand. The advertiser's name is cut to 'fG. BL NSHARD' and is read as G. Blanshard from the $20 reward notice two columns on, which prints it whole.

claims.notes: RULING 3'S VETO IN ITS PLAINEST FORM: the Eagle Hotel changes hands on 1 September 1834, from Paul J. Carli to J. Shrigley, and the notice says so in the paper's own words. The business record is made against the tavern and the claim carries `contradicts`, so the compiler holds Carli's tenancy as contradicted from this date rather than letting it stand into 1835. NO STREET is given for the Eagle Hotel here, so its placement class is 'none' and nothing is put on the plat from this claim.

claims.notes: THIS ISSUE REPRINTS THE 1 OCTOBER 1834 CHICAGO LETTER LIST, and its names are NOT minted here. The list runs from page 3 column 1 to the postmaster's signature in column 2, but the segmenter lost its opening: the heading survives only as the three lines quoted and the first name on the page is already at K. The issue of 1834-10-22 carries the same list whole and is where every name is minted — one list, one minting, which is the failure T-0299 records. Recorded here so that the reprint is on the record and the coverage assertion has something to point at.
